title: Slaughter and May Adopts Harvey Firmwide
author: Harvey Team

dom.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility

st.t: Power users: Usage volume may obscure value

It describes specialist rollout assistance and investment in people to supervise AI, while offering anticipated benefits rather than evidence of sustained use or measured outcomes.

kp.k: Firmwide rollout extends AI across legal practice areas
kp.d: The 2026 Harvey announcement reports that Slaughter and May is rolling out Harvey’s full platform across all practice areas, supporting lawyers on multi-jurisdictional M&A, due diligence, regulatory research and document analysis. This is an announcement of adoption and intended task coverage, rather than a report of measured outcomes.
qs: Slaughter and May, the leading international law firm, is rolling out Harvey’s AI platform firmwide.
The firm is adopting Harvey’s full platform across all practice areas to support its lawyers on multi-jurisdictional matters spanning M&A, due diligence, regulatory research, and document analysis.

kp.k: Human supervision and investment underpin adoption
kp.d: Managing Partner David Johnson, quoted by Harvey, frames firmwide adoption as enhancing client service and identifies investment in people as critical because they supervise AI. His stated model retains human oversight rather than presenting AI as an autonomous replacement for lawyers.
qs: Adopting Harvey firmwide allows us to enhance the excellent service that we provide to our clients. Critical to our adoption is the investment we make in our people, as the vital human layer that supervises AI.

kp.k: AI is positioned as amplifying collective legal expertise
kp.d: Sally Wokes, partner and Head of the firm’s Innovation Committee, argues that AI connects and applies the firm’s experience across situations, enhancing collective judgement, creativity and problem solving. This is the customer’s account of AI’s role, carried in the vendor announcement, not a quantified finding.
qs: Our differentiator is the depth and quality of our experience. AI allows us to connect and apply that expertise in different situations, enhancing the collective judgement, creativity and problem solving we bring to client matters.

kp.k: Selection combines agentic capabilities, security and client presence
kp.d: The announcement attributes Harvey’s selection to its agentic capabilities, security, experience with major law-firm AI transformation, presence across Slaughter and May’s client base and ability to meet the firm’s standards. These are reported selection rationales; the document supplies no specific capability tests or security assessment results.
qs: Harvey was selected for its agentic capabilities and security, its proven experience leading AI transformation inside major law firms, its presence across the firm’s client base, and its ability to meet the firm’s exacting standards.

kp.k: Vendor legal experts will support responsible implementation
kp.d: Harvey states that its Transformation Office, including legal experts, will work alongside Slaughter and May on the rollout. Responsible and effective adoption is presented as the objective of this implementation support, rather than an established outcome.
qs: Harvey’s Transformation Office, which includes seasoned legal experts, will work alongside the firm to support the rollout and ensure AI is adopted responsibly and effectively across the business.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Harvey reports a firmwide rollout at Slaughter and May to support legal work across practice areas; firm leaders describe AI as enhancing client service and lawyers’ application of expertise under human supervision.
pts.d: The Harvey Team announces adoption of Harvey’s full platform for multi-jurisdictional M&A, due diligence, regulatory research and document analysis. Managing Partner David Johnson claims firmwide adoption enables better client service, with investment in people and human supervision critical to adoption. Sally Wokes, partner and Head of the Innovation Committee, claims AI helps connect and apply the firm’s experience, enhancing collective judgement, creativity and problem solving. These are claims about augmentation of lawyers, not autonomous replacement. Harvey also states that its Transformation Office will support responsible and effective adoption.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers an adoption announcement, leadership testimony and asserted experience and selection criteria, rather than measured service improvements.
pts.d: The reported rollout is a concrete adoption example. Claims about benefits rest on statements by Johnson and Wokes and their descriptions of the firm’s expertise. The Harvey Team attributes selection to agentic capabilities, security, experience with major law firms, presence across the client base and meeting the firm’s standards. Harvey CEO Winston Weinberg invokes the firm’s historical combination of expertise and technology adoption. No data, benchmarks, completed-matter results or quantified changes in productivity, quality or cost are supplied.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The 2026 announcement describes a rollout underway and prospective implementation support, without a completion date or a timetable for benefits.
pts.d: The phrases “is rolling out” and “is adopting” indicate current implementation rather than a completed, evaluated deployment. The Transformation Office’s involvement is stated prospectively. Johnson explicitly identifies investment in people and human supervision as critical to adoption; Wokes situates the claimed benefits in the application of existing professional expertise. Agentic capabilities are cited as a selection factor, but the source does not specify the extent of autonomous task execution.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The stated effects concern Slaughter and May’s lawyers across all practice areas and clients receiving support on complex, multi-jurisdictional matters.
pts.d: Lawyers are the direct platform users and human supervisors, with AI presented as supporting their expertise and work. Clients are the intended beneficiaries of enhanced service, judgement, creativity and problem solving. Harvey’s Transformation Office provides implementation support across the business. The announcement concerns a major international law firm; it makes no specific predictions about staffing reductions, fees, market-wide displacement or access to justice.
